body.statement:
Every member of the parameterized late-ramp family lies in the baseline binary finite-population adaptive-design class described by Li and Zhao, but it does not satisfy their Gaussian Condition 3(ii). Consequently, if a sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over that larger baseline class, then, for each sign of every compatible late-ramp pair,
\[
 \liminf_n\Pr_\sigma\!\left\{
 \operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\delta(1-a_\star)\right\}
 \ge a_\star^c-2\alpha.
\]
This is a converse transfer by subclass inclusion only; it does not extend the positive profile-net calibration theorem beyond this note's structured binary profile subclass.
body.proof_tex:
The sourced statement \texttt{lem:li-zhao-baseline-adaptive-class} gives the relevant baseline-class requirements. For the binary parameterized ramp, define the two assignment probabilities by
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\frac ct,
 \qquad
 e_{nt}(0)=1-\frac ct.
\]
They are deterministic, hence prespecified functions of every allowed history. Because \(0<c<1\) and \(t\ge1\), both probabilities are strictly positive and their sum is one. Proposition \texttt{prop:parameterized-late-ramp-membership} proves that the potential outcomes are fixed and bounded and that \(m_{nt}(0)=m_{nt}(1)=0\) is predictable. The causal estimand is the finite-population treatment contrast. Thus every such array belongs to Li and Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.

We next verify failure of the additional Gaussian premise. In Li and Zhao's vector AIPW covariance, the control residual is identically zero, so the control row and column are zero and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\mathrm{aipw}})=0\). Hence Condition 3(ii), which requires the displayed inverse-eigenvalue expression to be \(o(1)\), is not satisfied. This is not merely an artifact of retaining the zero control coordinate. For the scalar treated-minus-control contrast, let \(W_n\) denote the corresponding scaled AIPW variance. Direct substitution of the deterministic residuals and \(e_{nt}(1)=c/t\) gives
\[
 W_n
 =\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n
   \left\{r^\sigma(t/n)\right\}^2
   \left(\frac{t}{c}-1\right).
\]
Writing \(u_t=t/n\), division by \(n\) yields
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}
 =\frac{\delta^2}{c(1-a_\star)^2}
   \frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n u_t(u_t-a_\star)_+^2
 -\frac{\delta^2}{(1-a_\star)^2}
   \frac1{n^2}\sum_{t=1}^n(u_t-a_\star)_+^2.
\]
The first sum is a Riemann sum and the second term is bounded in absolute value by \(\delta^2/n\). Therefore
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}
 \longrightarrow
 w_\star
 :=\frac{\delta^2}{c(1-a_\star)^2}
   \int_{a_\star}^1u(u-a_\star)^2\,du
 =\frac{\delta^2(a_\star+3)(1-a_\star)}{12c}>0.
\]
At \(t=n\), the outcome envelope is \(L_n=\delta\), the regression envelope is \(M_n=0\), and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the smallest binary assignment probability is \(\underline e_n=c/n\). Hence the scalar analogue of the Condition 3(ii) negligible-maximum ratio obeys
\[
 \liminf_n
 W_n^{-1}n^{-1}\max_{1\le t\le n}
 \frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}
 \ge \frac{\delta^2/c^2}{w_\star}
 =\frac{12}{c(a_\star+3)(1-a_\star)}>0.
\]
Thus the late ramp retains a nonnegligible standardized increment and lies outside the Gaussian Condition-3 regime, consistently with \texttt{lem:li-zhao-lindeberg-premise}.

Finally, uniform asymptotic honesty over Li and Zhao's baseline class implies the two-sign honesty premise of \texttt{thm:parameterized-late-ramp-frontier}, because both ramp laws form a subclass of that baseline class. Applying that theorem gives the displayed probability--diameter lower bound. This implication uses only subclass inclusion and therefore makes no assertion that this note's positive calibration theorem holds on the larger class.
body.justification: The proposition separates two claims that must not be conflated: baseline-class inclusion transfers the converse, while Condition-3 failure prevents invoking Li--Zhao's Gaussian theorem and does not enlarge this note's positive theorem.
body.gap: Without a sourced class comparison, the parameterized witnesses would establish only an analogue on a locally defined subclass.
body.consumer: Readers can apply the lower bound to any procedure advertised as uniformly honest over Li--Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.
